deities: Bodgeshwar (Kanakeshwar Baba), guardian deity of Mapusa

history.period: Tradition claims about 500 years old — weakly sourced (verify)
history.summary: The temple is dedicated to Bodgeshwar, also called Kanakeshwar Baba and locally Bodgini or Bongini, a guardian deity (Rakhandar) of Mapusa. He is regarded as an 'Angavani' — a deity to whom vows are made and who fulfills his devotees' desires — and is considered approachable by devotees of any faith. The temple grew around the worship of a banyan tree called 'Bogini' under which the deity was venerated. Legend holds that on moonless nights the torch of Bodgeshwar can be seen as he roams the paddy fields around the temple guarding Mapusa; townspeople once placed coconuts and beedis along his route. The annual Zatra fair in December/January draws thousands of devotees and tourists; some accounts credit the Bodgeshwar festival with Mapusa's growth as a market centre. One source (velpu.com) calls the temple 500 years old, but no dynasty, founder or date is documented — treat antiquity as unverified. The complex has two halls (AC and non-AC), a deepastambha, a big banyan tree and ample parking.

name: Shree Dev Bodgeshwar Temple
town_description: Mapusa is a municipal town in Bardez taluka, North Goa, about 12 km north of Panaji. It is best known for its bustling Friday market that draws vendors and shoppers from across North Goa. Though largely modern in appearance, it retains landmarks such as the Bodgeshwar temple on its outskirts — set amid paddy fields on the Calangute–Mapusa road — and the 1840s Maruti temple in its centre. The coordinates are approximate (taken from the temple's vicinity on the Calangute–Mapusa road).

travel.road: On the Calangute–Mapusa road on the outskirts of Mapusa, about 2 km from the Mapusa bus stand; about 12 km from Panaji by road
